data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_BOARD_TITLE
data.value: Applications board

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_BOARD_DESCRIPTION
data.value: The third view on the Applications page, a kanban board. Places applications arriving from e-mail and the extension on the board automatically, and fetches company logos from LinkedIn company pages every night (at most 50 pages a night).

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_BOARD_WHEN_OFF
data.value: The board view and the "On board" marker in the list are hidden; /api/board returns 404. Applications arriving while it is off are not placed on the board, and are not added later when it is switched back on. Logo fetching stops. Cards and logos are kept; the nightly job that removes closed cards after 14 days keeps running regardless.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_BLOG_TITLE
data.value: Blog and Guide

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_BLOG_DESCRIPTION
data.value: The public blog and guide articles, comments, likes, and the admin editor (including its AI SEO suggestion).

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_BLOG_WHEN_OFF
data.value: /blog and /guide return 404; the Blog and Guide links leave the menu, the header and the footer. Links to single guide articles on other pages (the help centre, the review guidelines, the flow card page) lead to the 404 page. The admin editor closes too; admins get 404 as well. Posts, comments and images are kept.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_BLOG_NOTES
data.value: On Google Cloud Storage it cannot be switched on without the blog image bucket (Storage:BlogMediaBucketName). The editor's "suggest with AI" button calls Vertex AI and costs money.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_COMPANY_REVIEWS_TITLE
data.value: Company reviews and company pages

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_COMPANY_REVIEWS_DESCRIPTION
data.value: The public company directory, company pages, writing and reading reviews, moderation and the My contributions list. Salaries, candidate experiences, silence reports and the Response tab sit on these pages.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_COMPANY_REVIEWS_WHEN_OFF
data.value: The company section closes: company pages return 404 and the /companies directory shows an "off" note; the Companies menu group and the Companies link in the header and footer are hidden, and the companies card on the landing page leads to that note. Salaries, experiences, silence reports and the Response tab disappear even with their own flags on. /contribute and My contributions show an "off" note too; the blog comments in My contributions are not listed meanwhile either. Reviews are kept.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_COMPANY_REVIEWS_NOTES
data.value: Salaries, Candidate experiences, Silence reports and the Company response tab depend on this flag.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_COMPANY_SALARIES_TITLE
data.value: Company salaries

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_COMPANY_SALARIES_DESCRIPTION
data.value: Users sharing salaries per company, and signed-in users reading salary bands on company pages.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_COMPANY_SALARIES_WHEN_OFF
data.value: The Salaries tab, the "Share salary" links and the salary prompts on the offer comparison and closing cards are hidden; the salary endpoints return 404. The company directory stops counting salary entries: companies whose only contribution is a salary drop out of the list. Entries are kept.

data.value: CV scan notes only work while this flag is on.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_CV_SCAN_NOTES_TITLE
data.value: CV scan AI notes

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_CV_SCAN_NOTES_DESCRIPTION
data.value: When the user separately consents, the CV text (first 15,000 characters) is sent to Google Vertex AI (EU region) for notes on the writing. The notes never change the score.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_CV_SCAN_NOTES_WHEN_OFF
data.value: The consent checkbox is hidden and no notes are produced. The score and findings work as before.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_CV_SCAN_NOTES_NOTES
data.value: Costs money (daily ceiling). The privacy policy (/privacy#cv-scan) names Vertex AI as a recipient; keep the flag and the text in step. Cannot be switched on without a Vertex project id (CvScan:Review:ProjectId). Needs the CV scan flag on.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_EMAIL_SIGNALS_TITLE
data.value: Gmail scanning (e-mail signals)

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_EMAIL_SIGNALS_DESCRIPTION
data.value: The extension reading job-application e-mails in Gmail and sending them to the server, and the status suggestions and notifications made from them.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_EMAIL_SIGNALS_WHEN_OFF
data.value: Every endpoint under /api/email-forwarding returns 404: the extension's submissions are refused, the Suggestions link and its counter leave the menu, /suggestions shows an "off" note, and Gmail updates leave the notification feed. Suggestions are kept; the nightly job that clears stale pending signals keeps running.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_EMAIL_SIGNALS_NOTES
data.value: When the rules cannot decide, the e-mail's subject and snippet go to OpenAI (United States); this costs money. The privacy policy and the extension privacy policy describe this flow; keep the flag and the text in step.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_EMAIL_AUTO_APPROVAL_TITLE
data.value: Apply e-mail suggestions automatically

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_EMAIL_AUTO_APPROVAL_DESCRIPTION
data.value: Applying high-confidence e-mail suggestions (at least 90% confidence, domain match, model decision) to the application status without asking the user. The user can undo it.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_EMAIL_AUTO_APPROVAL_WHEN_OFF
data.value: Suggestions wait for the user. With shadow mode on, the system only logs what it would have done. Changes already applied stay.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_EMAIL_AUTO_APPROVAL_NOTES
data.value: Has no effect while Gmail scanning is off.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_FEEDBACK_GIT_HUB_TITLE
data.value: Mirror feedback to GitHub

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_FEEDBACK_GIT_HUB_DESCRIPTION
data.value: Copying every in-app feedback entry into a private GitHub repository as an issue.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_FEEDBACK_GIT_HUB_WHEN_OFF
data.value: Feedback is stored in our own database only. Feedback sent while it is off is not mirrored when it is switched back on.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_FEEDBACK_GIT_HUB_NOTES
data.value: The privacy policy (/privacy#feedback, transfers abroad) names GitHub (United States) as a recipient; the flag and the text change together. Cannot be switched on without the repository and token.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_ATS_SOURCES_WHEN_OFF
data.value: A posting keeps only what the extension read from the page; Greenhouse postings are often left without a description. Reads already queued do nothing.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_ATS_SOURCES_NOTES
data.value: The extension privacy policy describes this second read; the flag and the text change together.

data.value: Weekly job matching (Pro)

data.value: What the Pro plan buys: postings collected from LinkedIn and kariyer.net every week, scored against the CV with Vertex AI (Gemini), and a digest e-mail.

data.name: FEATURE_FLAG_JOB_SOURCES_NOTES
data.value: Costs money (monthly budget). The privacy policy (/privacy#job-matching) describes this flow. Pro is sold only while this flag and Payments are both on.
